description:
Tech Alpha is a team of passionate technology enthusiasts interested in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, software development, and space exploration. We aim to combine technology, research, and creative storytelling to bring NASA's abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars back into the spotlight.

We are looking to build an interactive and innovative solution that explores the history, purpose, and stories behind these forgotten artifacts.
summary: Abandoned, but not Forgotten is an interactive web app that tells the stories of NASA hardware left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space, written for school-age space fans. Students choose a spacecraft, such as the Apollo 15 Moon Buggy, the Apollo 11 laser reflector, the Opportunity and Spirit rovers, the Ingenuity helicopter, the InSight lander or Voyager 1, and hear its story told in the first person, along with the science it made possible and a fun fact. A female AI voice can read each story aloud. Learners can see where each machine rests on a map of the Moon or Mars, compare distances and mission timelines, test themselves with a quiz, and chat with a spacecraft powered by the Groq AI model. The project answers the challenge by turning forgotten hardware into memorable characters, making real mission science easy to understand and inspiring the next generation of explorers.
details:
What it does: The app is a storytelling platform with six sections. Stories lets children meet seven NASA spacecraft in first-person “diaries”, with the science each one enabled and a fun fact. Where they rest maps each landing site on the Moon and Mars. Ask a spacecraft is an AI chat where students question a mission in simple language, and replies can be spoken aloud. By the numbers compares distances and mission timelines. Quiz checks what students learned. Team introduces Tech Alpha.

Why it matters: Hardware that has finished its mission is easy to forget. Giving each machine a voice and a story makes mission science memorable for children, and the quiz and map reinforce it.

How we built it: Python and Streamlit for the app, Pandas and Plotly for data and charts, Groq (Llama 3.3 70B) for the chat, and edge-tts for the female AI voice. The chat is instructed to use only our mission facts, answer in child-friendly language and stay on topic. Facts come from NASA mission pages.

Creativity and design: First-person storytelling, a “mission archive” visual design, voice narration, and a chat that lets children talk to a spacecraft.

Factors considered: Age-appropriate language, accuracy of facts, no API key needed for most features, free hosting on Streamlit Community Cloud.

SI use: See the SI section. Code was written with AI assistance, the chat and voice are AI-generated, and no NASA logos or branding are used.
